title: jQuery Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this jQuery course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does $("#title") return?
options: A jQuery collection of matching elements
questions.explanation: The jQuery function, often written $, selects page elements using a CSS selector. Its result is a jQuery collection.

questions.question: Which method writes plain text?
questions.explanation: The text method reads or replaces text. A replacement is treated as words rather than HTML markup.

questions.question: What value belongs in addClass?
questions.explanation: A class name lets CSS handle the appearance. jQuery can add or remove that name without rewriting the stylesheet.

questions.question: When does this handler run?
questions.explanation: The on method adds an event handler. It can run a function whenever the chosen element receives that event.

questions.question: Which method reads input text?
questions.explanation: The val method reads the current value of a form control. This is different from reading the text inside an ordinary paragraph.

questions.question: What reports the checkbox's live state?
questions.explanation: The prop method reads a live element property. A checkbox's checked property tells whether it is checked now.

questions.question: Which direction does closest search?
options: The element and then its ancestors
questions.explanation: closest walks up from an element until it finds a matching ancestor or the element itself. It is useful for finding the card that contains a button.

questions.question: Why use .text on the new item?
options: To run the title as JavaScript
To treat the title as plain text
questions.explanation: You can create an element and set its text before adding it to a list. This avoids building HTML from untrusted text.

questions.question: Where is the delegated listener attached?
options: On every future element automatically as a separate listener
questions.explanation: A delegated handler is attached to a parent and checks matching child elements. It can work for children added later.

questions.question: Why add .club to the event name?
options: To change the browser event into a CSS class
To remove this group of handlers precisely
questions.explanation: Event namespaces let you label handlers for later cleanup. off can remove just the handlers with that label.

questions.question: Which callback handles a failed request?
questions.explanation: getJSON makes a request for JSON data. done handles success, while fail handles a failed request.

questions.question: Which line works without loading jQuery?
questions.explanation: Many small jQuery jobs also have built-in browser equivalents. Understanding both helps maintain old code and write new code without unnecessary libraries.
